questions.a: 'was doing' — a specific past moment caught mid-action → past continuous. A wrong answer 'did' treats a film-moment as a snapshot.

questions.q: Fix: 'She is read her book now.'
questions.a: 'is reading' — continuous needs be + V-ing; 'is read' mixes forms. A wrong answer 'she reading' drops the be entirely — the helper is half the tense.

questions.q: Which is a snapshot and which a film: 'He wrote a letter' / 'He was writing a letter'?
questions.a: First = snapshot (completed), second = film (in progress). This single distinction drives every continuous-vs-simple choice in the class.

questions.q: ______ tenses add 'be + V-ing' to show action in progress: present continuous (is reading), past continuous (was reading), future continuous (will be reading).
Fill in the blank: Continuous tenses add 'be + V-ing' to show action in ______: present continuous (is reading), past continuous (was reading), future continuous (will be reading).
Fill in the blank: The film test: ______ = a movie playing, simple = a photograph. 'She was reading at 8' — film rolling at 8. 'She read the book' — snapshot, done.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student forms all three continuous tenses with correct be-forms, applies -ing spelling rules, and distinguishes continuous (in progress) from simple (habit/completed) in context.
